assumptions: Verified co-located Slurm profile: the real Helix client and Python/Nextflow controller share a root-controlled 1 CPU/2 GiB/swap-zero cgroup. All declared client work/temp/state/cache/export and remote workspace paths inherit one kernel XFS project quota. Worker tasks remain separate 2 CPU/2 GiB Docker allocations; no memory pooling.

Storage profile trp-colocated-client-storage/1.0.0 reserves32MiB overhead plus working-copy terms. This covers the real client/bootstrap/cache and portable export scope, calibrated on one development pilot before the aggregate campaign freeze; it is not a universal peak guarantee.
Two sequential tasks per traversal; one stub traversal then one real traversal; no retry or resume.
Task allocation: 2 CPUs/2 GiB. Controller allocation: 1 CPU/2 GiB; cgroup enforcement requires an independently verified operator sandbox. CPU bandwidth is not an exclusive core reservation.
Each traversal has an 8 minute watchdog; probes/configuration reserve another 120 seconds. This is a configured timeout, not a runtime prediction.

Storage estimates allocated workspace bytes including working copies, logs and portable evidence; an independently observed XFS project quota enforces an approved budget only inside an operator allocation.
The exact image and Nextflow distribution must already be cached. Image pulls/builds and shared Docker/Nextflow caches are outside workBytes.
Two remote scientific tasks are planned; SSH probes, controller commands and stub jobs are not scientific calls. Agent provider tokens, cost and conversation calls are not measured here.

limitations: Real Helix client and Python/Nextflow controller share the fixed controller cgroup; sequential worker tasks have separate Docker limits.
One XFS project covers declared client and NFS worker-visible work paths; preloaded read-only runtime/image caches and root supervisor records are outside workBytes.
Local Python transport on the verified head is explicit; this strict profile is not an SSH transport test. Worker memory is never pooled.
Allocated controller entitlement is not reduced by its own current usage. CPU quota is bandwidth, not exclusive cores.
